original.target_description: Nguyen et al., Experiment 3; American and Japanese final sample, independent and interdependent contexts; Experiment 3: perceived usefulness for eager and vigilant task performance of gain-framed versus loss-framed incentive structures; main effect of incentive structure. Bayesian mixed-effects model of within-culture standardized usefulness ratings.

n.sample_role: Participants in the analytic mixed-effects model (United States and Japan; both contexts)
n.exclusions: 18 American and three Japanese participants excluded. General exclusion criteria include distraction, low seriousness, language fluency, and MTurk location/repeated-location restrictions.

es.metric: βest (Bayesian coefficient; outcome standardized within culture)

replication.target_description: Vaughn et al., replication of American-independent conditions of Experiment 3; Experiment 3: perceived usefulness for eager and vigilant task performance of gain-framed versus loss-framed incentive structures; main effect of incentive structure. Within-subject 2 × 2 ANOVA.

n.sample_role: American participants in the final analytic repeated-measures sample
n.exclusions: One other participant excluded for taking less than one minute.
n.location: Study 3, Method—Participants; Table 1; Table 5 degrees of freedom
n.quote: Table 1 shows characteristics of the final sample (N = 101) of our replication of Nguyen et al.’s (2021) Study 3.

es.location: Replication of the American-Independent Conditions of Study 3, Conducted March 2022; Table 5 and omnibus ANOVA prose
es.quote: This main effect for incentives was very strong (ηp2 = 0.358; equivalent to d = 1.493).

p.location: Table 5, replication columns, corresponding predictor row

reported_success.quote: We replicated findings from the American-independent conditions of Nguyen et al.’s (2021) Experiment 3.

notes: Original results are the full cross-cultural model, not the American-independent reanalysis quoted secondarily in the replication. Original main-paper analyses are Bayesian and print HDIs rather than p values; no frequentist p has been attached to a Bayesian coefficient. Retrieved published pagination differs from the supplied locator. Replication d is explicitly printed by the authors (omnibus effects described as equivalent d); no conversion performed here. Replication incentives partial eta squared is .357 in Table 5 and 0.358 in prose; retained the prose’s printed d = 1.493. Reported success uses authors’ explicit study-level narrative replication verdict, not an inference from significance. Original prints Bayesian beta, not requested d.
